summary: The scripting language of the web browser. Netscape built it in 1995 to make pages interactive, it was standardised as ECMAScript two years later, and it now runs in every browser and, through Node.js, on servers too.

icon.licence: CC0 1.0 (the mark itself belongs to its owner)

events.note: Brendan Eich designs the language at Netscape, first called Mocha.
Ships in a Netscape Navigator beta under the name LiveScript.

events.label: Sent to Ecma
events.note: Netscape submits the language to Ecma International to become a standard.

events.label: Standard
events.note: The first ECMAScript specification is published.

events.label: ES3
events.note: ECMAScript 3 adds regular expressions and try/catch; it defines the language for a decade.

events.label: ES5
events.note: ECMAScript 5 adds strict mode and JSON support.

events.label: ES6
events.note: ECMAScript 2015 adds classes, modules, promises and arrow functions; yearly editions follow.

events.label: Free the name
events.note: An open letter asks Oracle to release the JavaScript trademark it inherited from Sun.
